Google\'s ML Kit on this device, made for photos and documents. Fast, but misreads comic lettering more often.
PaddleOCR\'s PP-OCRv6 on this device, which misread about a quarter as many words as ML Kit on test pages. Slower; the chapter\'s menu shows how long it took.
PP-OCRv6 unavailable, reading with ML Kit: %1$s
ML Kit finds the lines, and Baberu, a model trained on manga lettering, reads each bubble the detector found again. Needs the bubble detector. Downloads about 122 MB the first time; slow.
Baberu unavailable, reading with ML Kit only: %1$s
A detector on this device groups the text OCR read by the bubbles it finds, leaving out sound effects.
Gemini finds the speech bubbles and captions on each page image and translates them, leaving out sound effects and signs. Places text less precisely than the detector.
Only while Gemini translates. With another service, the detector finds the bubbles.
The text OCR read is grouped by its lines alone, without a detector, so sound effects are translated too.

OCR on this device reads the text, and Gemini looks at the pages and fixes what it misread before DeepL or another translator that can\'t see them translates it. Doesn\'t change who finds the bubbles. Uses the key and model below.
Lets a word too wide for its bubble break with only two letters on a side, as “CA-RAMBA”, when that makes the text much larger. Applies to pages opened after the change.
Pages keep their original text, and tapping a bubble shows its translation in a popup, closed by tapping outside it. Applies to pages opened after the change.
Bubble detector unavailable, grouping without it: %1$s
Queue each chapter for translation as soon as its download finishes. Pairs well with automatic downloads while reading.
